solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Head of Mafia caught by hired gun, surprisingly — wow!

definitions.note: a wow is a sensational thing, a noun as in 'the show was a wow'

indicators.note: the head letter is held inside the jumbled letters, as if taken prisoner
the letters of hired gun turn up in a surprising new order
the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A mob hitman unexpectedly nabs the Mafia boss, and the onlooker gasps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' scrambles HIRED GUN into HUDINGER, and 'caught by' puts M, the first letter of Mafia, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal nouns for something remarkable or outstanding, a real sensation.

clue.text: Sound of snake in bath is sinister

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words bath is sinister

explanation.surface: A snake's noise from the tub would be an ominous thing to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters sitting inside 'baTH IS Sinister'.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent makes a long sibilant sound, its characteristic noise.

clue.text: A home beneath me, most shabby

indicators.note: in a down answer, the later pieces sit below the first one

parts.note: taken as written
a nest is a bird's home, and by extension anyone's

explanation.surface: Someone says their flat below is the scruffiest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'beneath' puts A and NEST below ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean can describe something shabby or poor in quality; the superlative is the shabbiest.

clue.text: Sort fine material, discarding the first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the material is thrown away

parts.note: silk is a fine, luxurious fabric

explanation.surface: Someone sorts through fabric, throwing out the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean a kind or type, as in 'people of that kind'.

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the whole is read bottom to top
the witch swallows the knight, so he ends up inside her

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman, often a witch
a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A noisy witch devours a knight like a fairy-tale villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud' looks like volume but is the definition, in its sense of tastelessly bright; 'up' reverses the whole only because this is a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud colours are gaudy and showy, a synonym for tastelessly bright.

indicators.note: the words Large Miro are wrecked and put back together differently

explanation.surface: A big painting by Joan Miró has been vandalised, triggering a tiresome process.
explanation.walkthrough: Joan Miró was a Spanish surrealist painter; 'sabotaged' rearranges LARGEMIRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A long rambling or convoluted process, full of tedious formalities, is a classic synonym.

indicators.note: the word for the extra money comes back in the opposite direction

parts.note: a tip is extra money left for service

explanation.surface: Someone demands back a gratuity, claiming it is theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine!' looks like a claim of ownership but is the noun, a place dug for coal.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal mine is also called a colliery, an excavation in the ground.

definitions.meaning: to call someone is to ring them up
split in two, the answer reads ..., the reading of a very strong acid

explanation.surface: A chemist asks whether a sample is highly corrosive.
explanation.walkthrough: On the pH scale, low numbers mean strong acids, so a pH of one is very acidic.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is to make a telephone call to them.

clue.text: The boards are the best, ultimately for building

indicators.note: the ultimate, or final, letter of the word best
the letters are put together into a new structure

explanation.surface: Someone praises the best timber for construction work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives T from best; 'building' rearranges ARETHE plus T. 'The boards' is an idiom for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread the boards is to act on stage, so the boards stands for the stage and acting world.

indicators.note: the letters of clerk as are disorderly and get rearranged

explanation.surface: An unruly office clerk is a lazy, indifferent sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges CLERKAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirker who avoids work and effort is a lazy, indifferent person.

indicators.note: the phrase 'medication's hiding' means it has something concealed within the words

explanation.surface: A grumpy troll refuses his pills and hides them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' points to letters within 'takinG NO MEdication's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are small mythical creatures of folklore, so a troll is loosely the same sort of goblin.

clue.text: Where Romans found ten teams — went crazy

indicators.note: the letters of ten teams and went go mad and are scrambled

explanation.surface: Italian football fans saw ten teams play and went wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romans' suggests people of Rome but is the Epistle to the Romans, a book of the Bible; 'crazy' rearranges TENTEAMSWENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Romans is a Pauline epistle located in the later part of the Christian Bible.

clue.text: Couple of football teams, this is on the rugby pitch!

definitions.meaning: two sides of eleven players each make this total

definitions.text: this is on the rugby pitch!
definitions.meaning: a rugby pitch has a line marked this many metres from each try line

explanation.surface: A sports fan muses on two football sides and a rugby ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A rugby union pitch has a line marked at this many metres out from each try line.
explanation.definitionFit: Two elevens add up to this number of players; the rugby line is named for its distance in metres.

parts.note: utter means complete, as in 'utter nonsense'

explanation.surface: A golf club is now fully paged and ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer uses this short-hitting club on the green, so it is a type of club.

parts.note: pop is a fizzy soft drink such as lemonade
cheese in the sense of cheesy sentimental stuff is corn, as in corny

explanation.surface: A picnic menu offering a fizzy drink and a cheesy bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheese' looks like food but means trite or sentimental material, as in corny.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffed kernels of maize are eaten as a light snack, especially at the cinema.

indicators.note: the home contains the silver, packed inside it

parts.note: a domicile is a home
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A house stuffed with silverware commands admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay tribute or show honour to someone is a synonym of showing them respect.

clue.text: Traced new and old decorative style

indicators.note: the letters of traced are made new, in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone copied a design, mixing new and old ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like it describes the style, but it signals rearranging TRACED; 'and old' adds the abbreviation for old at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1920s and 1930s movement of geometric ornament in design and architecture is a decorative style.

definitions.meaning: a strong distilled alcohol such as whisky or gin
bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: A shopping list: a drink and a bottle to put it in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' looks like a container but is British slang for nerve, as in 'lose your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilled liquor is one sense; courage or mettle is another.

parts.note: pretty means quite, as in 'pretty good'
again, quite means pretty, as in 'pretty tired'

explanation.surface: Someone describes a thing as overly cute, twice for emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twee' is British for excessively cute or quaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something cloyingly dainty, prettified to the point of affectation.

parts.note: ex means former, describing something no longer in force
an act of parliament is a law

explanation.surface: A lawyer questions whether a strict statute has been struck off.
explanation.walkthrough: A repealed law is a former act, an ex-act.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise and strictly correct is the shared sense of the two adjectives.

indicators.note: the letters of diet are in a poor state and get reordered

explanation.surface: Advice to someone to alter an unhealthy eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges DIET.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise or amend text is to make changes to it.

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
a part is a section of something

explanation.surface: A segment of a ring designed in a contemporary fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1960s art movement using optical illusions is a modern style of art.

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of communists
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: Was the Tudor queen a Communist leader?
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth I of England famously had red hair; 'perhaps' marks her as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor queen had flame-coloured hair, so she is an example of a ginger-haired person.

definitions.meaning: A Spanish courtesy title for a gentleman
to put on clothes, as in donning a hat

explanation.surface: A Spanish honorific is adopted.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish nobleman's honorific is one sense; to dress oneself in clothing is the other.

definitions.meaning: a hard-shelled fruit like a walnut
someone cracked is crazy, an eccentric person or loony

explanation.surface: A tough piece of fruit has been split open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' looks like a broken shell but here means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-shelled kernel is one sense; a crazy person is another slang sense.

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
when joins two events as and does, as in 'dismissed when and dismissed'
twice calls for the word for dismissed a second time, so the first piece appears again

explanation.surface: A cricketer asks what the score is after being out in both innings.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a dismissed batter is out; being out once and then again is out and out.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete and utter, as in an out-and-out lie, is a sense of total.
